selection_signature_schema.purpose: Machine-friendly seed-selection metadata derived from template, axes, description, placeholders, and reasoning.

seeds.description: KPI sum for a specific calendar month (M1/M2/M3...M12)
seeds.reasoning: The phrase points to one specific completed calendar month rather than a span — cues like 'last month', 'M2', 'two months ago', 'three months back' all signal this pattern, and they're distinct from rolling-window or last-N-days phrasings. The 'M' index or the 'N months ago' phrase gives me N directly. Because the user is naming a single month and not a range, the date predicate uses exact equality: date_col = CurrentMonth-NMONTHS, not a >= comparison. The user is asking for a total, so the KPI column gets wrapped in SUM. The threshold value isn't fixed by the input — it's set at rule-creation time by the campaign manager — so I leave the right-hand side as ${operator} ${value} runtime placeholders. The assembled output is: date_col = CurrentMonth-NMONTHS AND SUM(kpi_col) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: KPI sum for rolling week 2-8 (bounded window with start/end day offsets)
seeds.reasoning: The phrase 'rolling week 2', 'W3', 'fourth rolling week' etc. signals a rolling-week band that is offset back from today, not a fixed calendar week. W2 through W8 are exact 7-day bands at fixed day-offsets: W2 = days 8-14 ago, W3 = 15-21, W4 = 22-28, and so on. So I need both bounds in days, not weeks: date_col >= CurrentTime-startDAYS AND date_col <= CurrentTime-endDAYS. The week index maps to a (start, end) pair from a lookup table. Because a rolling week is an event-aggregation band, I wrap the KPI in SUM. This is distinct from W1 which uses a different upper-bound style (< CurrentTime instead of <=), and from FIXED_WEEK which uses CurrentWeek-NWEEKS. Output: date >= CurrentTime-startDAYS AND date <= CurrentTime-endDAYS AND SUM(kpi_col) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: KPI sum for rolling week 1 (last 7 days, exclusive upper bound)
seeds.reasoning: Rolling week 1 is a special case: it's the most recent 7-day window, equivalent to 'the last 7 days rolling'. Unlike W2-W8 which use bounded day ranges with start/end offsets, W1 has a simple lower bound at CurrentTime-7DAYS and a strict upper bound of < CurrentTime. The strict less-than (rather than <= CurrentTime-0DAYS) is the distinguishing W1 convention — the partial current day is excluded. The KPI is wrapped in SUM as a 7-day rolling total. Final: date_col >= CurrentTime-7DAYS AND date_col < CurrentTime AND SUM(kpi_col) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: KPI sum over last N days (unbounded — no upper date limit)
seeds.reasoning: The phrasing 'in the last N days' / 'past N days' / 'over N days' with a numeric N signals an open-ended day window — start the range at CurrentTime-NDAYS and don't add an upper bound, since the user is implicitly including today. Because the user wants a cumulative figure ('total revenue', 'total recharge'), the aggregation is SUM. The key signal that distinguishes this from S05 is the absence of any 'excluding today' or 'completed days' phrasing — when those appear, the closed variant with < CurrentTime is needed. Output: date_col >= CurrentTime-NDAYS AND SUM(kpi_col) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: KPI sum over last N days with upper date bound (< CurrentTime)
seeds.notes: Airtel data usage uses this pattern. Omantel recharge uses this. The < CurrentTime upper bound is the key distinction from S04.
seeds.reasoning: This is the closed version of last-N-days: the user wants the last N days but excluding today's partial activity. The cue is either explicit ('the previous 30 days', 'past 7 days excluding today') or implicit (Omantel recharge KPIs where the engine convention is to use a closed bound). I need both bounds: >= CurrentTime-NDAYS at the start and < CurrentTime to cut off the current day. The KPI is wrapped in SUM for the closed-window total. The defining signal vs S04 is the presence of the < CurrentTime upper bound. Output: date >= CurrentTime-NDAYS AND date < CurrentTime AND SUM(kpi_col) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: KPI sum over last N days with upper bound AND not-null pre-filter
seeds.output_template: {date_col} >= CurrentTime-{N}DAYS AND {date_col} < CurrentTime AND {kpi_col} <> NULL AND SUM({kpi_col}) ${operator} ${value}
seeds.notes: Airtel-specific. Note N is offset by 1 (31 for 30-day window). Has <> NULL pre-filter on KPI.
seeds.reasoning: This is the Airtel-specific closed last-N-days pattern. Two telltale features: a not-null guard on the KPI (Airtel data-usage rows can be sparse with nulls that would otherwise be summed as zeros incorrectly), and an N value that is offset by +1 vs the natural-language span (a 30-day window uses N=31, 7 days uses N=8, etc.) to align with Airtel's exclusive-boundary convention. I assemble: lower bound >= CurrentTime-NDAYS, upper bound < CurrentTime, then a kpi_col <> NULL pre-filter, then SUM(kpi_col) for the windowed total. Output: date >= CurrentTime-NDAYS AND date < CurrentTime AND kpi_col <> NULL AND SUM(kpi_col) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: KPI sum for current month to date
seeds.reasoning: Month-to-date phrasing — 'this month', 'so far this month', 'current month', 'MTD' — maps to a single calendar predicate using exact equality on CurrentMonth. The engine reads date_col = CurrentMonth as 'any event whose date falls within the current calendar month'. No N offset, no upper bound — MTD is implicitly bounded by today. The KPI is wrapped in SUM for the running month total. Output: date_col = CurrentMonth AND SUM(kpi_col) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: KPI sum for last month to date (>= previous month)
seeds.reasoning: Last-month-to-date is an open range that begins at the first of last month: it's not a complete-month equality (that would be S01 with N=1), it's an inclusive cumulative figure starting from one month ago. Phrases like 'LMTD', 'same period last month', 'previous month to date' map here. The single date predicate is >= CurrentMonth-1MONTHS — open-ended, no upper bound — and the KPI is wrapped in SUM. The distinction from S01 is critical: S01 uses '=' for one fixed month, S08 uses '>=' for a running total since the start of last month. Output: date_col >= CurrentMonth-1MONTHS AND SUM(kpi_col) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: Simple SUM without any time filter
seeds.reasoning: When the user asks for a lifetime or all-time total — 'overall total revenue', 'lifetime IDD revenue', 'aggregate to date' — there is no time predicate at all. Just SUM the KPI column without any date filter. This pattern is rare and only used for cumulative lifetime values where the underlying table itself is already scoped (e.g. a snapshot table). Output: SUM(kpi_col) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: SUM with not-null pre-filter, no time window

input_phrases: total recharge amount where recharge exists

seeds.reasoning: The user wants a SUM but only over rows where the KPI is non-null — a pre-filter is required. Cue phrases: 'recharge sum where recharge exists', 'revenue where revenue is recorded'. No time window. The pattern is two clauses: kpi_col <> NULL as a row-level guard, then SUM(kpi_col) on the surviving rows. The null guard prevents the engine from miscounting rows where the KPI never had a value. Output: kpi_col <> NULL AND SUM(kpi_col) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: SUM with > 0 pre-filter, no time window

input_phrases: prepaid voice revenue for active voice users

seeds.reasoning: Similar to S10 but with a stricter pre-filter: only sum over rows where the KPI is strictly positive. This is used for PayG-style revenue checks where zero values shouldn't be considered 'active' usage. Cue: 'voice revenue for active voice users', 'data PayG revenue'. The pre-filter kpi_col > 0 ensures only non-zero rows enter the SUM. Output: kpi_col > 0 AND SUM(kpi_col) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: Raw KPI value (no SUM) for a calendar month — Airtel ARPU
seeds.reasoning: This is an Airtel ARPU pattern — a single calendar month, but no SUM aggregation because ARPU is already a per-row computed value. Cue: 'last month ARPU', 'monthly ARPU'. Use date_col = CurrentMonth-NMONTHS for the month equality, then compare the kpi_col directly without wrapping in SUM. The distinction from S01 is the absence of the SUM wrapper. Output: date_col = CurrentMonth-NMONTHS AND kpi_col ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: KPI sum over last N months with upper bound (< CurrentMonth) — Airtel data usage
seeds.notes: Airtel. Note this adds NOT NULL filter: {kpi_col} <> NULL. Distinct from S50/S51 formula patterns.
seeds.reasoning: A closed range over the last N completed calendar months. Phrases: 'last month' (N=1), 'previous calendar month'. The closed pattern is >= CurrentMonth-NMONTHS and < CurrentMonth, ensuring only fully completed months are counted. The KPI is wrapped in SUM. Note that for Airtel, this is data usage and a not-null guard is added (per the seed notes). Output: date >= CurrentMonth-NMONTHS AND date < CurrentMonth AND SUM(kpi_col) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: Average KPI computed as SUM(col/N) with virtual formula over month range

input_phrases: average ARPU over the last 3 months
average recharge over the last 3 months

seeds.reasoning: The user wants the average of a KPI over the last N completed months. Cue: 'average ARPU over last 3 months', 'average recharge across 3 months'. The engine doesn't have a windowed AVG, so I express 'average over N months' as a virtual KPI formula: V{vp_name}=f{kpi_col/N}, then SUM that virtual divided value across the N-month window. The window is closed: >= CurrentMonth-NMONTHS AND < CurrentMonth. Output: date >= CurrentMonth-NMONTHS AND date < CurrentMonth AND SUM(V{vp_name}=f{kpi_col/divisor}) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: Average KPI computed with virtual formula over completed week range

input_phrases: average weekly data free revenue over the past 4 weeks
average data free revenue over the last 4 completed weeks

seeds.reasoning: The phrasing 'average weekly X over the past 4 weeks' is asking for an average over a closed range of completed weeks. Two clauses are needed for the time window: >= CurrentWeek-NWEEKS to start the range, and < CurrentWeek to ensure only completed weeks are counted (the current partial week must be excluded). For the average itself, the rule engine doesn't have a native AVG over a window — instead it uses a virtual KPI formula V{vp_name}=f{kpi_col/divisor} where divisor equals N. So I express 'average across N weeks' as 'sum of (kpi_col / N)' wrapped in SUM. Final shape: date >= CurrentWeek-NWEEKS AND date < CurrentWeek AND SUM(V{vp_name}=f{kpi_col/N}) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: Average KPI computed with virtual formula over day range (no upper bound)

input_phrases: average recharge over the last 90 days

seeds.reasoning: Average computed over a 90-day day-window using the virtual formula trick. This is the day-unit cousin of S14. The window starts at CurrentMonth-90DAYS (note: month-anchored start, not CurrentTime-anchored — that's the engine convention here) and runs open-ended. The average is encoded as SUM(V{vp_name}=f{kpi_col/divisor}). Output: date_col >= CurrentMonth-90DAYS AND SUM(V{vp_name}=f{kpi_col/divisor}) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: Virtual formula combining multiple KPI columns with addition

input_phrases: combined incoming and outgoing call minutes
combined IDD call and SMS revenue
total IDD revenue combining calls and SMS

seeds.reasoning: The user wants a virtual KPI computed by adding two columns — typical cases: incoming + outgoing call MOU, IDD call rev + IDD SMS rev. Cue: 'combined X and Y', 'sum of X plus Y', 'total X and Y'. The pattern needs per-column positive guards (col1 > 0 AND col2 > 0) so the sum isn't polluted by zero rows, then a virtual KPI formula SUM(V{vp_name}=f{col1+col2}) that the engine will materialize as a single derived column. No time window in this base variant. Output: col1 > 0 AND col2 > 0 AND SUM(V{vp_name}=f{col1+col2}) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: Virtual formula combining 5 PayG revenue columns

input_phrases: total PayG revenue combining all channels

seeds.reasoning: Same multi-column-addition pattern as S16, but with five PayG revenue columns combined. All five columns get individual > 0 guards, then the virtual formula sums them: V{vp_name}=f{col1+col2+col3+col4+col5}. The five-column structure is specifically for the consolidated 'total PayG revenue billing' VP. Output: col1 > 0 AND col2 > 0 AND col3 > 0 AND col4 > 0 AND col5 > 0 AND SUM(V{vp_name}=f{col1+col2+col3+col4+col5}) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: Social media volume sum combining 4 app columns with time window
seeds.reasoning: Combine four social-media app volume columns (WhatsApp + Facebook + TikTok + Instagram) into a single 'total social media volume' over a time window of N days. Unlike S16/S17 which have no time predicate, this one adds >= CurrentTime-NDAYS for the window. The virtual formula sums the four columns. No per-column > 0 guards in this variant (the engine handles missing app columns differently for SM patterns). Output: date >= CurrentTime-NDAYS AND SUM(V{vp_name}=f{col1+col2+col3+col4}) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: GEX revenue with unit conversion virtual formula
seeds.reasoning: GEX revenue with a unit conversion built into a virtual formula — divide by 1,000,000 to convert from raw to OMR. Cue: 'GEX revenue in OMR', 'GEX amount converted'. The pattern is a > 0 pre-filter on the KPI plus a virtual formula V{vp_name}=f{kpi_col/1000000}. The 1000000 divisor encodes the unit conversion explicitly in the rule rather than relying on a separate transform. Output: kpi_col > 0 AND SUM(V{vp_name}=f{kpi_col/1000000}) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: Recharge amount with virtual formula conversion
seeds.reasoning: Recharge amount checked through a virtual formula multiplication (often *1, identity transform that triggers the engine's virtual-KPI evaluation path). Pre-filters: kpi_col > 0 and date_col <> NULL to exclude unrecharged or undated rows. The virtual formula V{vp_name}=f{(kpi_col*1)} then has > 0 as the comparison. The slightly odd pattern exists because some downstream consumers require a virtual-KPI form even when no real transform is needed. Output: kpi_col > 0 AND date_col <> NULL AND V{vp_name}=f{(kpi_col*1)} > 0.

seeds.description: DPI usage filtered by protocol/app for current month
seeds.reasoning: MTD pattern (S07) plus a protocol filter for DPI usage. Cue: 'streaming data usage this month', 'YouTube volume current month'. Three clauses: date_col = CurrentMonth, filter_col = filter_val (e.g. dpi_app_usage_protocol = 'Streaming'), then SUM(kpi_col). The filter scopes the SUM to one app or protocol within the current month. Output: date_col = CurrentMonth AND filter_col = filter_val AND SUM(kpi_col) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: DPI usage filtered by protocol for last N days

input_phrases: streaming usage in the last 30 days

seeds.reasoning: Open last-N-days DPI usage with a protocol filter. Cue: 'streaming usage in the last 30 days'. Combines S04's open day-window with S21's protocol filter. Three clauses: date >= CurrentTime-NDAYS, filter_col = filter_val, SUM(kpi_col). Output: date >= CurrentTime-NDAYS AND filter_col = filter_val AND SUM(kpi_col) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: DPI existence check (SUM > 0) for current month

input_phrases: has any streaming usage this month
has any data usage this month
has any YouTube usage this month
has any YouTube streaming usage this month

seeds.reasoning: DPI existence check for the current month — does the subscriber have ANY usage of a particular type. Cue: 'has any streaming usage this month', 'streaming data exists this month'. Differs from S21 by hardcoding > 0 as the comparison rather than a runtime ${operator} ${value} — because 'has any' is semantically a presence check, not a threshold. The filter_conditions clause varies by sub-variant (some use protocol = Streaming, some use protocol+subport, etc.). Output: date_col = CurrentMonth AND filter_conditions AND SUM(kpi_col) > 0.

seeds.description: Product subscription presence — not null + count > 0
seeds.reasoning: Product subscription presence — confirms the subscriber currently has an active product. Three clauses: id_col <> NULL (the product column has a value), id_col ${operator} ${value} (typically =, with the product ID supplied at runtime), and COUNT_ALL > 0 (at least one matching subscription record). The triple-clause form is the engine's idiomatic 'has product' check. Output: id_col <> NULL AND id_col ${operator} ${value} AND COUNT_ALL(id_col) > 0.

seeds.description: Product subscription absence — not null + count = 0

input_phrases: is not subscribed to a product

seeds.reasoning: Counterpart to S24 — product subscription absence. Same three clauses but with COUNT_ALL = 0 instead of > 0. The id_col <> NULL guard is still there because the engine needs the column to be a candidate before checking that no matching rows exist. Output: id_col <> NULL AND id_col ${operator} ${value} AND COUNT_ALL(id_col) = 0.

seeds.description: Action key count = 0 (never sent)

input_phrases: subscriber has not received the action key

seeds.reasoning: Generic action-key absence check with no time window. Cue: 'action key was never sent', 'subscriber has not received the action key'. Two clauses: a key match {key_col} ${operator} ${value} (so the rule can target a specific action key at runtime), then COUNT_ALL = 0 to confirm zero occurrences. The absence of any date predicate means this is a lifetime check. Output: key_col ${operator} ${value} AND COUNT_ALL(key_col) = 0.

seeds.description: Action key count > 0 (sent at least once)

input_phrases: action key was sent at least once
subscriber has received the action key

seeds.reasoning: Lifetime action-key presence — counterpart to S26. Same two clauses with COUNT_ALL > 0 instead of = 0. Cue: 'action key was sent at least once', 'subscriber has received the action key', 'action key exists'. Output: key_col ${operator} ${value} AND COUNT_ALL(key_col) > 0.

seeds.description: Action key absent within a time window

input_phrases: subscriber did not receive the action key

seeds.reasoning: Action-key absence within a time window — combines S26 with a date predicate. Cue: 'no action key in last 15 days'. Three clauses: key match, date >= CurrentTime-NDAYS for the window, and COUNT_ALL = 0 for absence in that window. Output: key_col ${operator} ${value} AND date >= CurrentTime-NDAYS AND COUNT_ALL(key_col) = 0.

seeds.description: Action key present within a time window
seeds.reasoning: Time-scoped action-key presence — counterpart to S28 with COUNT_ALL > 0. Cue: 'action key sent in last 7 days', 'received in past week'. Three clauses: date window first, then key match, then COUNT_ALL > 0. The order of date/key matters in some engines; here the date predicate appears first, then the key match, then the count. Output: date >= CurrentTime-NDAYS AND key_col ${operator} ${value} AND COUNT_ALL(key_col) > 0.

seeds.description: Subscription count at most N within 30 days
seeds.reasoning: Subscription count capped at a threshold within 30 days. Cue: 'at most 1 product subscription in the last 30 days', 'no more than 2 subscriptions'. Three clauses: a fixed 30-day window, key match, then COUNT_ALL <= threshold. The threshold is a discrete value (1, 2, 3, 4) and is hardcoded into the rule, not runtime — that's the differentiator from a generic <= ${value} check. Output: date >= CurrentTime-30DAYS AND key_col ${operator} ${value} AND COUNT_ALL(key_col) <= threshold.

seeds.description: Subscription count = 0 within N days

input_phrases: not subscribed in the last 30 days
not subscribed in the last 40 days

seeds.reasoning: Subscription absence (count = 0) within a time window of N days. Cue: 'not subscribed in the last 30 days', 'no subscription in last 40 days'. The structure is the same as S28 but for product subscriptions specifically. Output: date >= CurrentTime-NDAYS AND key_col ${operator} ${value} AND COUNT_ALL(key_col) = 0.

seeds.description: Column not null + count check
seeds.reasoning: Generic existence-by-count check on a column — the column has a non-null value AND the count of rows is in some range. Cue: 'HBB addon exists', 'whitelist entry exists', 'activation date exists'. Two clauses: count_col <> NULL pre-filter, then COUNT_ALL with the runtime ${operator} ${value} threshold. Distinct from S26/S27 by the runtime threshold (vs hardcoded = 0 / > 0) and by the not-null guard. Output: count_col <> NULL AND COUNT_ALL(count_col) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: Action key count check for today (near real-time)

input_phrases: action key sent exactly once today
action key sent exactly twice today
action key sent exactly 3 times today
action key sent less than 2 times today

seeds.reasoning: Near-real-time action-key check on the current day. Cue: 'action key sent today', 'no action key today', 'action key sent twice today'. Three clauses: date = CurrentTime (exact current-day equality), key match, and COUNT_ALL with one of several count directions: = 0, = 1, = 2, = 3, < 2. The current-day equality and the multi-valued count direction are the distinguishing features. Output: date_col = CurrentTime AND key_col ${operator} ${value} AND COUNT_ALL(key_col) {count_dir}.

seeds.description: Action key check with date <= CurrentTime

input_phrases: action key has never been sent up to now
no action key sent to date
action key has been sent at some point

seeds.reasoning: Lifetime action-key check with date <= CurrentTime — useful for 'has the key ever been sent up to now' semantics. Three clauses: key match, date <= CurrentTime, and COUNT_ALL with either = 0 (never sent historically) or > 0 (sent at some historic point). The <= CurrentTime is a no-op upper bound that exists for engine compatibility. Output: key_col ${operator} ${value} AND date <= CurrentTime AND COUNT_ALL(key_col) {count_dir}.

seeds.description: Action key check at exact date offset
seeds.reasoning: Action-key check at an exact date offset — e.g. 'exactly 180 days ago' or 'within the last 180 days'. The date operator can be either = (exact) or > (within), depending on phrasing. Three clauses: date {= or >} CurrentTime-NDAYS, key match, COUNT_ALL > 0. Output: date_col {= or >} CurrentTime-NDAYS AND key_col ${operator} ${value} AND COUNT_ALL(key_col) > 0.

seeds.description: Action key count capped at threshold

input_phrases: action key sent at most 2 times

seeds.reasoning: A simple frequency-cap pattern: action key sent at most N times. Cue: 'frequency cap of 2', 'sent at most 2 times'. No date predicate, no other guards — just a key match and COUNT_ALL <= threshold. Distinct from S30 because there's no 30-day window scoping; this is a lifetime cap. Output: key_col ${operator} ${value} AND COUNT_ALL(key_col) <= threshold.

seeds.description: Simple COUNT_ALL without any filters
seeds.reasoning: Bare COUNT_ALL with no filters — just count rows of a column and compare against a runtime threshold. Cue: 'SSO recharge count', 'total transaction count', 'number of transactions'. Single clause. The simplest possible count check. Output: COUNT_ALL(col) ${operator} ${value}.

seeds.description: Simple COUNT_ALL = 0 for subscriptions (no key filter)
seeds.reasoning: Subscriber has zero subscriptions overall — a COUNT_ALL = 0 with no other clauses, not even a key filter. Cue: 'subscriber has zero subscriptions', 'no active subscriptions at all'. The absence of a key match means this counts ALL subscription rows, not a specific product. Output: COUNT_ALL(key_col) = 0.

seeds.description: Promotion delivered — LC_ACTION_TYPE = Promotion, count > 0
seeds.output_template: {date_col} >= CurrentTime-{N}DAYS AND LC_ACTION_TYPE IN LIST (Promotion;PROMOTION;promotion) AND {key_col} ${operator} ${value} AND COUNT_ALL({count_col}) > 0
seeds.reasoning: The user wants subscribers who received a promo within a recent window. 'Delivered' / 'received' / 'campaign reached subscriber' all signal a presence check (count > 0), not absence. The 'last N days' phrase means I need a date window with >= CurrentTime-NDAYS. Because this is specifically about promotions and not bonuses, the LC_ACTION_TYPE column needs a filter to the promotion variants — and since the data uses mixed casing (Promotion, PROMOTION, promotion), I use IN LIST with all three. The action key match {key_col} ${operator} ${value} lets the rule target a specific campaign at runtime. Finally, COUNT_ALL on the count column with > 0 confirms at least one delivery happened. Output: date >= CurrentTime-NDAYS AND LC_ACTION_TYPE IN LIST (Promotion;PROMOTION;promotion) AND key_col ${operator} ${value} AND COUNT_ALL(count_col) > 0.

seeds.description: Promotion not delivered by action key — count = 0
seeds.output_template: {date_col} >= CurrentTime-{N}DAYS AND LC_ACTION_TYPE IN LIST (Promotion;PROMOTION;promotion) AND {key_col} ${operator} ${value} AND COUNT_ALL({count_col}) = 0

input_phrases: promotion was not delivered for action key
promo not sent by action key
promotion was not delivered for segment

seeds.notes: Covers both action key (L_ACTION_KEY) and segment (LC_SEGMENT_NAME) variants — same skeleton when column names are replaced.
seeds.reasoning: The mirror of S39 — promotion was NOT delivered to a subscriber for either an action key or a segment. The structure is identical to S39 except COUNT_ALL flips to = 0 for the absence semantic. The same three components are needed: a date window, the LC_ACTION_TYPE IN LIST filter for case variants of 'Promotion', and the key/segment match. Two sub-variants exist (action key vs segment name) but they collapse into the same template once the column names are substituted. Output: date >= CurrentTime-NDAYS AND LC_ACTION_TYPE IN LIST (Promotion;PROMOTION;promotion) AND key_col ${operator} ${value} AND COUNT_ALL(count_col) = 0.

seeds.description: Bonus non-responder — LC_ACTION_TYPE = BONUS, count = 0
seeds.output_template: {date_col} >= CurrentTime-{N}DAYS AND LC_ACTION_TYPE IN LIST (BONUS;Bonus;bonus) AND {key_col} ${operator} ${value} AND COUNT_ALL({count_col}) = 0

input_phrases: subscriber did not respond to bonus for action key
subscriber did not respond to bonus for segment

seeds.reasoning: Bonus non-responder pattern — same skeleton as S40 but the action type filter targets BONUS variants instead of Promotion. Cue: 'subscriber did not respond to bonus', 'bonus non-responder by action key'. Replace the action-type IN LIST with (BONUS;Bonus;bonus). Everything else (date window, key match, COUNT_ALL = 0) is identical. The case variants matter because the underlying data has all three forms. Output: date >= CurrentTime-NDAYS AND LC_ACTION_TYPE IN LIST (BONUS;Bonus;bonus) AND key_col ${operator} ${value} AND COUNT_ALL(count_col) = 0.

seeds.description: Promo sent check with groupby and Max date verification
seeds.output_template: {date_col} >= CurrentTime-{N}DAYS AND {key_col} ${operator} ${value} AND COUNT_ALL({count_col})__groupby_{key_col} > 0 AND Max({date_col}) <> NULL
seeds.reasoning: Promo presence with deduplication and date-confirmation. Cue: 'promo was sent and confirmed', 'promotion sent with date verification'. Four clauses: date window, key match, COUNT_ALL grouped by key with > 0 (which dedupes across action keys), and a Max(date_col) <> NULL clause that verifies the latest send-date exists. The __groupby_ suffix and the Max guard together encode 'unique by key with confirmed latest date'. Output: date >= CurrentTime-NDAYS AND key_col ${operator} ${value} AND COUNT_ALL(count_col)__groupby_key_col > 0 AND Max(date_col) <> NULL.

seeds.description: Bonus absent — count < 1 (not zero, using less-than)

input_phrases: subscriber has not received any bonus

seeds.reasoning: Bonus absent variant that uses < 1 instead of = 0 for the count comparator. Functionally equivalent to '= 0' but stylistically different — some rules express absence as 'less than 1' rather than 'equals zero'. Three clauses: date window, key match, COUNT_ALL < 1. The < 1 is the diagnostic feature vs S26/S28. Output: date >= CurrentTime-NDAYS AND key_col ${operator} ${value} AND COUNT_ALL(count_col) < 1.

seeds.description: Action key OR CG variant absent — groupby count = 0

input_phrases: bonus action key or CG variant has not been processed
bonus with action key or control group not received

seeds.reasoning: Action key OR control-group variant absent — used when a campaign has both a treatment key and a CG (control group) key, and the rule needs to check that NEITHER was processed. seeds.description: Product presence for product list in a pinned previous month

seeds.reasoning: Used for product purchase/subscription presence in a specific pinned month, e.g. last month, two months ago, or the month that was N months ago.
